The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx) was a scientific initiative by Harvard University aimed at understanding the behavior of aerosol particles in the stratosphere. Principal investigator Frank Keutsch and his team publicly discussed the project, highlighting its role in improving computer models to assess the risks and benefits of solar geoengineering. Importantly, SCoPEx was not designed to deploy geoengineering techniques or cool the planet, but rather to gather data on aerosol microphysics and chemistry.

The experiment involved a scientific balloon gondola releasing a tiny amount of material—such as calcium carbonate—into a controlled volume. However, a planned test in 2021 was suspended to prioritize societal engagement, reflecting a commitment to transparent governance and public accountability. As of March 2024, Keutsch has stepped back from pursuing SCoPEx, and the platform is set to be repurposed for unrelated stratospheric research. This development reinforces the need for rigorous dialogue around geoengineering and emphasizes that any approach must prioritize climate justice and emissions cuts over unproven solutions. #climateaction #climatejustice #mitigation #geoengineering
